subject: Request: carveout for customer-managed edge impacting latency SLO
messages:
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos@valencebio.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Cc: ops@valencebio.com
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Carveout request: customer-managed edge causing latency spikes

Hi Naomi,

We hit recurring tail-latency incidents last quarter where our real-time genomics pipelines saw request latencies spike intermittently (10-20% of samples) due to our edge transit. Those spikes are outside our engineering window to troubleshoot without service disruption. Because Valence controls the edge router/NAT and a portion of the transit path, we need Redwood to accept an SLA exception for latency attribution when the root cause is on our side.

Specifically we propose: if packet loss > 1% at the customer edge or if downstream traceroutes show >300ms additional hop latency attributable to our network appliances, Redwood would exclude those incidents from Redwood's latency SLO breach calculations.

I've attached a sample packet capture and a short incident timeline from May 9–11. Can we get a list of what evidence Redwood will need and whether you can provide a temporary telemetry export so we can jointly verify? We'd like to avoid a full contract amendment; a signed appendix or playbook would be ideal.

Thanks,
Carlos Mendez
Head of Infrastructure, Valence Bio
Attachments: packet-trace-20280512.pcap (pcap, 2.6MB)
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos@valencebio.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Carveout request: customer-managed edge causing latency spikes

Carlos — thanks for the detail and the packet capture. This is the right level of specificity.

High-level response and next steps:
- We can define a scoped "Customer Edge Attribution" carveout that excludes incidents where evidence indicates the customer-controlled network is the primary cause.
- Evidence we would require (one or more of):
  * synchronized packet captures (pcap) showing retransmits/packet loss at the edge,
  * traceroutes showing consistent >300ms hop at the customer-controlled hop across >=5 representative probes,
  * BGP session flaps or interface counters demonstrating sustained loss.
- Operational expectations: Valence will enable NetFlow or similar and grant read-only telemetry access for the carveout period. If telemetry is not available, carveout requests require a 48-hour joint analysis window before exclusion is accepted.
- Timebox: we recommend a 6-month pilot with monthly review; after that we can convert to a standing appendix or revert.

I've drafted a short appendix (attached) that maps categories, evidence requirements, and reporting cadence. Legal (Marissa) and Product (Aditya) are looped in — Marissa please call out any redlines; Aditya can confirm feasibility of dashboard exports and the fallback plan to hosted routing if necessary.

If this looks reasonable we can route DocuSign and start the telemetry hookup.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Customer Success Lead — Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Attachment: sla-edge-exception-draft.pdf (proposal, 14 pages)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Carlos Mendez <carlos@valencebio.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 May 2028 09:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Carveout request: customer-managed edge causing latency spikes

Thanks Naomi and Carlos — quick legal notes on the draft appendix:
- We should make the pilot explicit (6 months) with an automatic review at 90 days. If either party wants to terminate the carveout early, include a 30-day notice provision.
- Add a clause requiring Valence to provide read-only telemetry (NetFlow / sFlow / packet captures) and a point of contact available during post-incident analysis windows. If telemetry is not provided, Redwood reserves the right to deny exclusion requests for those incidents.
- Limit the carveout to attribution for latency breaches only; uptime and data durability SLAs remain Redwood's responsibility except where direct evidence shows customer-managed network caused service interruption.
- Add an indemnity-lite paragraph limiting Redwood's liability for incidents caused solely by customer-managed components.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

P.S. Aditya — can your team confirm whether Redwood can export a 30-day rolling latency dashboard to the customer's Azure workspace? We should make the telemetry export and dashboard part of the operational acceptance criteria in the appendix.
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos@valencebio.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 18 May 2028 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Carveout request: customer-managed edge causing latency spikes

Naomi / Marissa — appreciate the quick turnaround and the draft. Valence is comfortable with a 6-month pilot and the evidence requirements you outlined. A couple of small asks before we sign:
1) Confirm Redwood will surface an aggregated latency dashboard (30-day window) and a weekly summary report during the pilot.
2) Valence will enable NetFlow and provide read-only access; we ask Redwood to confirm telemetry onboarding checklist and an estimated 5 business day window to validate access.

If you can confirm those two items in the appendix, we'll route via DocuSign and get our Infra team to start the NetFlow export this week.

Carlos Mendez
Head of Infrastructure, Valence Bio
Attachments referenced: none in this reply
